front_blocks.md: Define **economies of scale**.

back_blocks.md: **Economies of scale** are the efficiencies a business gains as it grows, which **lower its average (unit) costs** of production.

cards.front_md: Define **economies of scale**.
cards.back_md: **Economies of scale** are the efficiencies a business gains as it grows, which **lower its average (unit) costs** of production.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Economies of scale lower a business's total costs.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
They lower **average (unit) costs**, not total costs — total costs still rise, but at a **decreasing rate per unit**.

cards.front_md:

cards.back_md:
**False.**

front_blocks.md: What is the difference between internal and external economies of scale?

back_blocks.md: **Internal** economies lower costs when the **business grows**; **external** economies lower costs when the **whole market/industry grows**.

cards.front_md: What is the difference between internal and external economies of scale?
cards.back_md: **Internal** economies lower costs when the **business grows**; **external** economies lower costs when the **whole market/industry grows**.

front_blocks.md: Define **purchasing economies of scale**.

back_blocks.md: **Purchasing economies** occur when large firms **buy in bulk** and receive **discounts**, lowering the average cost per unit.

cards.front_md: Define **purchasing economies of scale**.
cards.back_md: **Purchasing economies** occur when large firms **buy in bulk** and receive **discounts**, lowering the average cost per unit.

front_blocks.md: What are managerial economies of scale?

back_blocks.md: When large firms can afford **specialist, highly skilled managers**, whose greater efficiency **lowers average costs**.

cards.front_md: What are managerial economies of scale?
cards.back_md: When large firms can afford **specialist, highly skilled managers**, whose greater efficiency **lowers average costs**.

front_blocks.md: Name two internal economies of scale.

back_blocks.md: **Purchasing** economies and **managerial** economies.

cards.front_md: Name two internal economies of scale.
cards.back_md: **Purchasing** economies and **managerial** economies.

front_blocks.md: Name two external economies of scale.

back_blocks.md: A **better-skilled workforce** and **improved infrastructure**.

cards.front_md: Name two external economies of scale.
cards.back_md: A **better-skilled workforce** and **improved infrastructure**.

front_blocks.md: How does a better-skilled workforce create external economies of scale?

back_blocks.md: A growing industry concentrates **skilled workers** who need **less training** and become **productive quickly**, lowering costs.

cards.front_md: How does a better-skilled workforce create external economies of scale?

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Bulk-buying raw materials is an example of a purchasing economy of scale.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Buying in **greater volume** earns **bulk discounts**, reducing the **cost per unit**.

front_blocks.md: What happens to average costs once a firm grows beyond its minimum-cost level of output?

back_blocks.md: They **start to rise again** as **diseconomies of scale** occur.

front_blocks.md: Define **diseconomies of scale**.

back_blocks.md: **Diseconomies of scale** are the reasons a firm's **average costs rise** as it grows **too large**.

cards.front_md: Define **diseconomies of scale**.
cards.back_md: **Diseconomies of scale** are the reasons a firm's **average costs rise** as it grows **too large**.

front_blocks.md: What happens to average costs when a firm grows beyond its optimal size?

back_blocks.md: **Average costs start to rise** because of **diseconomies of scale**.

cards.front_md: What happens to average costs when a firm grows beyond its optimal size?
cards.back_md: **Average costs start to rise** because of **diseconomies of scale**.

front_blocks.md: Name three causes of diseconomies of scale.

back_blocks.md: **Poor communication and coordination**, **increased bureaucracy**, and a **lack of commitment from employees**.

cards.front_md: Name three causes of diseconomies of scale.
cards.back_md: **Poor communication and coordination**, **increased bureaucracy**, and a **lack of commitment from employees**.

front_blocks.md: How does poor communication cause diseconomies of scale?

back_blocks.md: As a firm grows, the **chain of command lengthens**, so communication becomes **slower** and mistakes worsen efficiency, raising costs.

cards.front_md: How does poor communication cause diseconomies of scale?
cards.back_md: As a firm grows, the **chain of command lengthens**, so communication becomes **slower** and mistakes worsen efficiency, raising costs.

front_blocks.md: How does increased bureaucracy cause diseconomies of scale?

back_blocks.md: Larger firms are **more complicated to run**, needing extensive **administration**, staff and resources that raise average costs.

cards.front_md: How does increased bureaucracy cause diseconomies of scale?
cards.back_md: Larger firms are **more complicated to run**, needing extensive **administration**, staff and resources that raise average costs.

front_blocks.md: Why might employees become less committed as a business grows?

back_blocks.md: They may feel **less valued** with limited management contact, becoming **demotivated**, which lowers output and raises average costs.

back_blocks.md: The point at which a firm can no longer reduce its costs any further is called productive **efficiency**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Diseconomies of scale mean a business can become so large that it becomes less efficient.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Beyond a certain size, problems such as poor communication make a business **less and less efficient**.

front_blocks.md: How might a business reduce diseconomies of scale?

back_blocks.md: By **reconsidering its organisational structure** — e.g. breaking into **smaller autonomous units** to improve communication.
